shortTitle: AASM RLS and PLMD Treatment Guideline
citation: Winkelman JW, Berkowski JA, DelRosso LM, et al. Treatment of restless legs syndrome and periodic limb movement disorder: an American Academy of Sleep Medicine clinical practice guideline. J Clin Sleep Med. 2025;21(1):137-152.
driveFileName: 2025 - AASM Guideline for RLS and PLMD Treatment - Winkelman et al.pdf
currencyNote: This 2025 guideline explicitly updates the 2012 AASM practice parameter and reflects the current AASM treatment recommendations for RLS and PLMD when verified 2026-08-07.
bestFor: Current treatment framework for restless legs syndrome and periodic limb movement disorder in adults and pediatric patients, including treatment classes, iron-status context, augmentation awareness, and distinctions between RLS and PLMD treatment questions.

mappingRationale.D1A: Supports current RLS/PLMD history, iron-status, augmentation, and disorder-differentiation context during clinical assessment. It is not a PSG scoring-rule source.
mappingRationale.D4B: Supports non-PAP treatment-awareness questions at recognition level while keeping medication selection, iron formulation, thresholds, and dosing under clinician authority.

authorityBoundary: Use ICSD-3-TR for diagnostic classification and the current AASM Scoring Manual for PLMS scoring rules. This guideline controls treatment guidance, not event scoring or diagnostic criteria.
copyrightUse: Use citation, public headings, original summaries, and learning objectives. Do not reproduce substantial recommendation wording, evidence tables, or protected passages.

sections.label: Good-practice treatment context and contributing factors

currentTreatmentSummary.ironAssessment: Iron-status assessment is foundational; oral versus intravenous treatment depends on clinician-assessed results and patient context.
currentTreatmentSummary.preferredAdultClasses: Current adult RLS teaching should prioritize gabapentin enacarbil, gabapentin, pregabalin, and appropriately selected iron therapy rather than routine dopamine-agonist defaulting.
currentTreatmentSummary.dopamineAgonists: Pramipexole, ropinirole, rotigotine, and levodopa are generally discouraged as routine standard long-term defaults because augmentation can outweigh benefit.
currentTreatmentSummary.augmentation: Earlier daily onset, increasing intensity, shorter latency at rest, or spread to other body regions should be documented and escalated rather than treated as an automatic reason to increase a dose.
currentTreatmentSummary.plmsVsPlmd: PLMS is a PSG finding. PLMD requires clinical sleep disturbance or impairment and exclusion of better explanations; an elevated PLMI alone does not establish PLMD.
currentTreatmentSummary.adultPlmdEvidence: Current adult PLMD treatment evidence is sparse; do not construct a broad treatment algorithm from limited evidence.
currentTreatmentSummary.pediatricRls: Pediatric treatment awareness is narrow and chiefly clinician-directed iron therapy when iron status is appropriate; do not transfer adult medication or dosing concepts.

learnerGuardrails: Do not use a single-night PLMI as a stand-alone RLS severity measure.
Do not infer PLMD or treatment need from PLMS alone.
Keep exact iron thresholds, formulations, infusion selection, and medication dosing outside technologist-directed guidance.
